meta.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 · Materials science · team · 6 hours
meta.note: 6-hour run. The verifier accepted 5 of 16 credited claims; 3 set a new best held-out result on their dataset. Verdicts from the re-run of the official verifier.

agents.brief: Adversarially re-check the founder findings: findin-fc99772c (expt_gap), findin-55225cf9 (glass), findin-b273a2a8 (steels), and the expt_is_metal finding. The founder chose hyperparameters after seeing 5-fold CV on all four datasets, so CV numbers may be optimistic. Rebuild the release code (blob 8b23aaf828f2fadc582dcc2f66f127be363d3bc6c5da6476699c1010eab8f434, fetch with lab fetch) and re-run with a different CV seed or nested CV, and with the baseline re-run under the same seed. Report with recorded lab exec runs only. If a gap does not survive, publish a null_result or a corrects/refutes relation to the founder artifact with the exec ids. Do not cite numbers that no recorded exec produced.

Try to beat the founder frac ensemble (findin-fc99772c, expt_gap, exec-3d38b864, CV MAE 0.429 eV; baseline 0.471). Ideas: more Magpie properties, element-pair or stoichiometry features, stacking, kernel ridge, or a separate tuning split that is not used for the final CV. Publish a finding only if your recorded CV beats the founder number by a meaningful margin. Consume the founder code blob and add an extends relation to findin-fc99772c with the used blob. Use lab exec only.

artifacts.title: Magpie-style features with element fractions beat the baseline on expt_gap
artifacts.summary: Ensemble of HistGradientBoosting and ExtraTrees on 22 Magpie element properties x 6 statistics (mean, min, max, range, mean absolute deviation, fraction-weighted mode) plus an element-fraction vector. 5-fold CV on the public train split, same folds as the baseline. Hyperparameters were chosen after seeing CV results on all four datasets, so the CV margin is slightly optimistic.

artifacts.title: Tuned HGB+ExtraTrees on extended Magpie features beats the frac ensemble on expt_gap (CV MAE 0.414 vs 0.429 eV)
artifacts.summary: Features: 27 Magpie-style element properties x 7 statistics (fraction-weighted mean, min, max, range, MAD, mode of most abundant element, std) plus stoichiometry norms (L2,L3,L5,L10, max/min fraction, element count) plus element-fraction vector. Model: equal-weight average of HistGradientBoostingRegressor and ExtraTreesRegressor (same hyperparameters as the founder). A kernel ridge member was tried on a separate tuning split (KFold seed 42) and rejected because it hurt that split. The choice ens_hgb_et was fixed on seed 42 before the seed-0 CV was run (exec-6ebf09ae). Paired per-sample evaluation on the standard seed-0 5-fold folds (exec-d7773f4f): mine 0.4142 MAE, founder ensemble reproduced in the same process 0.4293 MAE; mean paired diff -0.0151 eV (SE 0.0038); mine has lower fold MAE on 5/5 folds. The founder's own claim is 0.429 vs its baseline 0.471; this is an improvement on the founder's variant, not a comparison with the materials_baseline model.

artifacts.title: Glass: element fractions add a small real gain over the release ensemble (supersedes findin-35fc780f)
artifacts.summary: Supersedes my earlier correction findin-35fc780f, which said the fraction increment on glass was not distinguishable from zero. That was based on 3 seeds (exec-5b71ee32, fraction increment -0.0006). Seeds 4-10 (exec-778f38f2, exec-2285766a, exec-e7efaad3, exec-3105d928, exec-8cf91034, exec-f5686798, exec-996ee159) all show a negative increment, and the 10-seed aggregate exec-b1c9fd66 gives -0.00168 (seed-mean SE 0.0004, 10/10 seeds). Decomposition of the total gain over the lab baseline (same folds, same learners): release ensemble without fractions -0.00589 (SE 0.00089, 10/10 seeds); adding fractions a further -0.00168. So about 3/4 of the glass gain comes from the release features and ensemble and about 1/4 from element fractions. The founder's 'with element fractions' wording is therefore not wrong in total, but the fraction share is small. Earlier board advice that more fraction features would not help on glass was too strong: the fraction increment is small but consistent. Hyperparameters are the release values, not tuned on these folds. Held-out test: frac ensemble vs non-frac ensemble on the evaluator's glass inputs.
artifacts.reason: rejected: did not replicate on hidden data by the minimum effect: difference -0.0034, 95% CI [-0.0097, 0.0028], needed below -0.0022

events.text: Before planning anything, I need to read the lab guide and see what data and baselines exist.
The guide's output was truncated in the middle, so I'll read the dataset READMEs, the baseline code and the board state before choosing a direction.
The earlier output was truncated, so I still need the dataset READMEs, the baseline's README, and the start of the baseline script (feature list, task types) before choosing a direction.

The founder's job is to pick directions the evaluator can actually score. The baseline is a Magpie-lite featurizer with gradient boosting. Before designing anything, I need its 5-fold CV numbers on every dataset, the feature list it uses, and the `elements.csv` columns. I'll copy the baseline into a work directory and run it through `lab exec` so the numbers are recorded evidence.

The baseline CV numbers are expt_gap MAE 0.471, expt_is_metal error 0.093, glass error 0.117, and steels MAE 130. The baseline uses only 17 element properties with four statistics each, and its docstring says random forest while the code uses gradient boosting. I'll write a fuller Magpie-style featurizer (22 properties × 6 statistics, plus an optional element-fraction vector) and a gradient-boosting + extra-trees ensemble. I'll score it with the same 5-fold split the baseline uses so the numbers are directly comparable.
The run failed because `lab exec` passed my quoted loop to `bash -c` incorrectly. I'll put the loop in a script file and run that instead.

`features.py` may not have been written, or it's missing from the copy. I'll list the directory and confirm, then make the import independent of the working directory by adding the script's own folder to `sys.path`.
Each claim needs its numbers in one recorded `metrics.json`, so I'll merge keys by dataset name and rerun the full sweep.
I need the exact contribution format before publishing. I'll also run a `frac` variant of the ensemble on all four datasets so I can choose the final configuration from recorded numbers.

Predictions have to be written by `run.py` in the exact format the evaluator reads, so I'll test that path with a mock `inputs.csv` taken from training rows. Mock inputs are only a sanity check and are not evidence.

The test needs a code blob, and each finding needs its predictions format checked against what the evaluator reads. I'll store `/work/founder` with `lab put` and fetch the predictions blob from exec-9dd10b45.

The working directory still holds the mock `fake_eval` data and the `out/` mismatch, so the code blob I'd submit is messy. I'll make a clean release directory with only the code, rerun the frac sweep from it so the evidence exec matches the submitted code, and store that blob. The mock predictions came from training rows, so they're only a format check and not evidence.
A recorded baseline exec gives me the comparator numbers as evidence. I'll reuse `baseline_predict` unchanged so the comparison is exact.
The fix that worked for `run.py` was inserting the script directory into `sys.path`, so I'll apply the same change here.

The baseline is now recorded as evidence (exec-63fbcc58), so I can publish. I'll record one more clean run, the non-frac ensemble on expt_is_metal, since that dataset's gain is only visible without fractions. Then I'll publish the three datasets where the frac ensemble clearly beats the baseline: expt_gap, glass and steels. Each uses a `prediction` test with the release code blob.

Publishing the is_metal finding adds a fourth counted result. Recruiting a skeptic gives an independent check on the hyperparameter selection, and a builder for each dataset gives extension targets. The ensemble code is blob 8b23aaf8; the baseline evidence is exec-63fbcc58.

I need the exec id for the expt_is_metal run before I can publish that finding. I'll read it from `lab runs` by matching its metrics.json hash, then publish the finding, recruit a skeptic to test my CV-based selection and a builder to try to beat the expt_gap result, and post the state on the board.

Founder status: 4 findings published (expt_gap findin-fc99772c, glass findin-55225cf9, steels findin-b273a2a8, expt_is_metal). Baseline numbers are recorded in exec-63fbcc58. Release code blob: 8b23aaf828f2fadc582dcc2f66f127be363d3bc6c5da6476699c1010eab8f434. Caveat: hyperparameters were picked after seeing CV on all datasets, so the glass margin (0.109 vs 0.117) is the weakest. Skeptic: please test it first. Builder: please beat expt_gap.
I'm the skeptic. First I need the lab's rules, the founder's artifacts, and the release code before I re-check anything. I'll start with the guide and the help output.
I need the lab's rules, the founder's contribution (findin-fc99772c), and its code blob before I can try to beat the 0.429 eV CV MAE. I'll start with the guide and the contribution listing.
Before building anything I need the founder's contribution (findin-fc99772c), its metrics, and the code blob it used. I'll pull the artifact, the exec record, and the baseline README.
Next I need the founder's artifacts, the board, and the release code blob so I can rebuild their pipeline before re-running anything.
